name: Bivamelagon
lead: Bivamelagon (also LB54640) is an investigational oral melanocortin 4 receptor (MC4R) agonist. [1][2] It is being studied in hypothalamic obesity, weight gain following damage to the hypothalamus, and is not an approved drug.

A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 trial in acquired hypothalamic obesity was reported in the Journal of the Endocrine Society in 2025. [1] A registered phase 2 study (n=28) finished, and a long-term extension study (n=25) began enrolling by invitation in November 2025. [2][3]

paras: The phase 2 trial in acquired hypothalamic obesity tested once-daily oral bivamelagon against placebo. [1] The registry listing NCT06046443 began in July 2024 and is complete, and NCT07156578 is a long-term follow-up. [2][3] No studies were found in healthy people seeking cosmetic fat loss.

timeline.event: Phase 2 study in hypothalamic obesity begins. [2]
Phase 2 results presented; long-term study starts. [1][3]

card.summary: Investigational oral MC4R agonist tested for hypothalamic obesity; no data in cosmetic use.
card.note: Not approved; studied only in a rare medical obesity.

quick.overview:
Bivamelagon is an experimental once-daily oral drug that activates the MC4R, a brain receptor involved in appetite and weight regulation.

It has been tested in a phase 2 trial in people with hypothalamic obesity. It is not approved.
quick.mechanism: It stimulates MC4R signaling in the brain's weight-regulating pathway.
quick.risks: Not approved anywhere; safety data are limited to early trials in a small patient group.
